en: Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at the Bamboo Grove Monastery in Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of his fourfold disciples, for whom he was preaching the Dharma.
At that time, in the kingdom of Vaiśālī, a pestilence was raging with fierce intensity.
It was like a blazing fire where countless people had died, finding no refuge and no means of remedy.
Thereupon, Ānanda knelt down with palms joined and addressed the Buddha, saying: "In that country of Ayodhyā, a pestilence of hot vapors has struck;

I only pray that the World-Honored One will expound various holy arts to repel that toxic vapor, so that they may attain peace and security and be freed from all suffering and affliction. The Buddha told the worthy one:
"Ānanda, you should listen and receive this: there are seven spirits who constantly emit poisonous vapors to harm the myriad people.
If a person encounters their poison, they suffer headaches, chills, and fevers; the hundred joints ache, and the pain is difficult to describe.
If anyone knows their names, the poison will not harm them. Therefore, I shall now speak of them for you. Ānanda said, "I wish to hear it."
I have heard the Buddha say that if the fourfold assembly of disciples wishes to invoke the names of spirits and deities for the purpose of bringing peace, they should at that time say:
"Namo Buddhāya! Namo Dharmāya! Namo Saṃghāya! Namo to all Buddhas of the ten directions!
Namo to all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas! Namo to all Noble Saṃghas! Namo to the Master of Mantras [Name]! Now I..."
The divine spell spoken by the disciple shall fulfill his wish; such is the name of this deity, which I shall now proclaim.
Having recited "Śarākha" three times, he then spoke the mantra: [Mantra follows]
The many-difficulty ghosts, the Akhani ghosts, the Nikhaśi ghosts,
the Akhana ghosts, the Parani ghosts, the Abhira ghosts,
and the Pratiri ghosts.

The Buddha said: "These are the names of the seven spirits and deities for this incantation. If a person suffers from a feverish illness, one should call upon the names of these seven spirits and deities, saying:
'Depart quickly! Depart quickly! Do not remain long! Cause the poison to be extinguished within my disciple’s body and let the illness be swiftly cured!
My disciple now takes refuge in the Triple Gem, burns incense, pays homage, and practices according to the teachings of all Buddhas."
If there are any deities of the incantations herein spoken who do not follow the teachings of the Buddha, their heads shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.

If a person falls ill with a feverish affliction for one day, two days, three days, or even up to seven days, first consecrate divine water with this incantation and give it to the patient to drink; one should recite this incantation scripture twenty-one times.

All diseases caused by the five types of poisons shall be completely extinguished. Furthermore, if one establishes a gate and records the ailments of wind-disorders (*vāta*), one should write the names of the seven spirits upon its lintel.
Then, taking threads of the five colors, tie knots for each of those names and fasten them to the top of the gate;
this brings great auspiciousness. If one can diligently recite this sutra, single-mindedly uphold it, and observe the precepts of fasting and abstinence—
If one eats pungent spices and recites the names of these seven spirits, the *ūnaviṃśati* ghosts will be permanently severed and shall not pass through one's door;
they will instead advance to the house of the afflicted, and upon seeing them, all the ghosts will flee, such that one’s person will never again be defiled by celestial plagues.

If one can focus the mind and exhort others to copy, receive, uphold, and recite this sutra, calamities will be eliminated and harms repelled. If one is unable to recite it, [one should write it] on bamboo tubes.
If one places this on the lintel of the main gate, the *wēn* ghosts will not dare to pass through the door; it shall also bring longevity, nourishment, and great auspiciousness.
Ānanda joined his palms and addressed the Buddha, saying, "What should this sutra be named, and how should it be upheld?
The Buddha said, "This sutra is named 'The Divine Incantation for Warding Off *Wēn*. Thus spoke the Buddha. When the assembly of devas, nāgas, spirits, and all others heard this, they rejoiced."
The *Dhāraṇī of the Joyful One*, to be recited with reverence and practiced accordingly.
*The Sutra of the Re-warming Divine Dhāraṇī*.
